PNG 501: This course provides students with fundamental skills to formulate problems of fluid flow in porous media in the context of reservoir engineering applications.
PNG 502: This course is a foundational course in the study of unsteady problems of flow, deformation, and transport in porous media.
PNG 511: Differencing schemes for the partial differential equations of single-phase flow; application to flow of gas and mixing in porous media.
PNG 512: Mathematical analysis of complex reservoir behavior and combination drives; numerical methods for the solution of behavior equations; recent developments.
PNG 518: Theory and design of miscible methods of oil recovery, current field applications, including hydrocarbon, CO2, micellar/polymer, alkaline, and inert gas.
PNG 520: Thermodynamic science applied to hydrocarbon mixtures and problems in petroleum and natural gas engineering.
PNG 526: Causes and identification of oil and gas wells with low productivity and or recovery; design and evaluation of well stimuation methods.
PNG 530: Flow in producing or storage reservoirs; gas well testing; transmission systems; storage cycle; current developments.
PNG 555: This course provides an in-depth analysis of the technical aspects of unconventional oil and gas reservoirs, such as geochemistry, geomechanics, storage mechanisms, and transport processes.
PNG 566: This course focuses on the quantitative characterization of oil and gas reservoirs, principally through analysis of seismic survey data, well logs, and by employing geostatistics.
PNG 577: In petroleum and natural gas engineering, production and completion operations are critical components of field development operations.
PNG 590: Continuing seminars that consist of individual lectures by faculty, students or outside speakers on energy and mineral engineering issues.
PNG 596: Creative projects, including nonthesis research, which are supervised on an individual basis and which fall outside the scope of formal courses.
PNG 597: Creative projects, including nonthesis research, which are supervised on an individual basis and which fall outside the scope of formal courses.
PNG 598: Formal courses given on a topical or special interest subject which may be offered infrequently; several different topics may be taught in one year or semester.
